test_title: PYST 37: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 21 Feb, 2025 - Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: Ajit and Bimal can do a piece of work in 5, and 8 days, respectively, while Chandan can destroy the same work in 12 days. Ajit works on the 1st day, Bimal works on the 2nd day, Chandan works on the 3rd day and so on. They follow the same pattern until the work gets completed. How many days will it take for the work to be completed the first time?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM(5, 8, 12) = 120 units.

1 cycle (3 days) work = Ajit + Bimal + Chandan = 24 + 15 − 10 = 29 units.

Work completed in 3 full cycles (9 days) = 3 × 29 = 87 units.

On 10th day, Ajit adds 24 units ⇒ Total work = 87 + 24 = 111 units.

Remaining 9 units are done by Bimal on 11th day in 9 ÷ 15 = 3/5 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 ³/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Ajit = 5 days

Time taken by Bimal = 8 days

Time taken by Chandan (destroying work) = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Ajit
 5
 120
 24
 
 

 Bimal
 8
 15
 
 

 Chandan
 12
 −10
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in a 3-day cycle = 24 + 15 − 10 = 29 units.

⇒ In alternating positive-negative work, reserve the peak positive capacity to avoid over-calculating.

⇒ Peak positive continuous work in a cycle = 24 (Ajit) + 15 (Bimal) = 39 units.

⇒ Work to complete safely using full cycles = 120 − 39 = 81 units.

⇒ Number of full 3-day cycles needed = 81 ÷ 29 ≈ 2.79 ⇒ safely take 3 full cycles.

⇒ Work done in 3 cycles (9 days) = 3 × 29 = 87 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 120 − 87 = 33 units.

⇒ On the 10th day, Ajit works and completes 24 units.

⇒ Work left after 10 days = 33 − 24 = 9 units.

⇒ On the 11th day, Bimal works. Time taken by Bimal = 9 ÷ 15 = 3/5 day.

⇒ Total time taken = 10 + 3/5 = 10 ³/₅ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 ³/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternating Work with Negative Efficiency

When positive and negative work alternate, always subtract the maximum positive continuous work from the total work. Use the remaining work to find the number of full cycles needed to safely approach completion without exceeding the total work.

Total Work using LCM

For multiple individuals working at different rates, Total Work is assumed to be the LCM of their individual time to ensure calculations remain in whole numbers, and Efficiency is calculated as Total Work ÷ Time.
